Surah Az-Zumar (The Groups), Meccan except verses 52, 53 and 54, which are Medinan. It has 75 verses and was revealed after Saba'.

﴿The revelation of the Book﴾ — the Qur'an, the subject (mubtada'); ﴿from Allah﴾ — its predicate (khabar); ﴿the Almighty﴾ — in His dominion; ﴿the All-Wise﴾ — in His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 2:

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you﴾ O Muhammad ﴿the Book in truth﴾. "In truth" is connected to "sent down." ﴿So worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ from polytheism; i.e., affirming His oneness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 3:

﴿Surely, to God belongs the pure religion.﴾ None other deserves it. ﴿As for those who take protectors besides Him,﴾ [i.e., who worship idols] ﴿"We worship them only that they may bring us nearer to God in closeness."﴾ [They are the disbelievers of Makkah, who said this.] Zulfa (closeness) is a verbal noun (masdar) meaning taqrib (bringing near). ﴿Surely God will judge between them﴾ and between the Muslims ﴿concerning that about which they differ﴾ regarding matters of religion, so that the believers enter Paradise and the disbelievers enter the Fire. ﴿Surely God does not guide one who is a liar﴾ in attributing offspring to Him, ﴿an ungrateful disbeliever﴾ by worshipping other than God.

﴿Had God wished to take a son,﴾ as they said: ﴿"The All-Merciful has taken a son,"﴾ ﴿He would have chosen whatever He wills from what He creates.﴾ And He would have taken as a son other than those they mentioned: the angels, who they said were the daughters of God; Uzayr, whom they said was the son of God; and the Messiah, whom they said was the son of God. ﴿Glory be to Him!﴾ (exalting Him above having taken a son). ﴿He is God, the One, the Subduer﴾ over His creation.

﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾: [the phrase] "in truth" is connected to "created."

﴿He wraps﴾ means He makes ﴿the night enter over the day﴾, so that it increases [in length]. ﴿And wraps the day﴾ means He makes it enter ﴿over the night﴾, so that it increases [in length].

﴿And He subjected the sun and the moon, each running﴾ in its orbit ﴿for a specified term﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Unquestionably, He is the Mighty﴾, who prevails over His affair, ﴿who takes vengeance on His enemies﴾, ﴿the Forgiving﴾ toward His friends.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 6:

﴿He created you from a single soul﴾, i.e., Adam. ﴿Then He made from it its mate﴾, Hawwa' (Eve). ﴿And He sent down for you of the cattle﴾, the camels, cows, sheep and goats, ﴿eight kinds﴾ (lit. "eight pairs"), of each two spouses, male and female, as explained in Surat al-An'am. ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾, i.e., first as nutfah (a drop of fluid), then 'alaqah (a clinging clot), then mudghah (a lump of flesh). ﴿In three darknesses﴾: the darkness of the belly, the darkness of the womb, and the darkness of the placenta. ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. There is no god but He, so how are you turned away﴾ from His worship to the worship of other than Him.

﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is Free of need of you, and He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾, and [He does not approve it] even if He wills it for some of them. ﴿And if you are grateful﴾ to Allah by believing, ﴿He approves it for you﴾, read with the ha' of ﴿يَرْضَهْ﴾ having sukun, with damma, with damma and lengthening (ishbaa'), and without lengthening, i.e., the gratitude. ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾, i.e., no soul [shall bear] the burden of another soul; ﴿it does not carry it﴾. ﴿Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾, i.e., what is in the hearts.

﴿When harm touches the human being﴾, i.e., the disbelieving person, ﴿he calls upon his Lord﴾, humbling himself, ﴿turning back﴾, returning ﴿to Him. Then, when He bestows upon him a blessing﴾, granting him a favour ﴿from Him, he forgets﴾, abandons ﴿what he used to call upon﴾, where ﴿ما﴾ (what) stands in place of ﴿مَن﴾ (whom), ﴿before﴾, and that is God, ﴿and sets up rivals﴾, partners ﴿to God, to lead astray﴾, with the yā' (ي) of ﴿لِيُضِلّ﴾ read with a fatḥah (بِفَتْحِ الياء) or with a ḍammah (وضَمّها), ﴿from His way﴾, the religion of Islam. ﴿Say: Enjoy your disbelief for a little while﴾, the remainder of ﴿your term﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 9:

﴿Is he who is devoutly obedient⟩ (amman), with the mim lightened; and in another reading, am man, where am means "rather" (bal) together with the hamza. ﴿huwa qanit⟩ means standing in the duties of obedience. ﴿Through the hours of the night⟩ means its periods. ﴿Prostrating and standing⟩ in prayer. ﴿Fearing the Hereafter⟩ meaning he fears its punishment, ﴿and hoping for the mercy⟩ meaning Paradise, ﴿of his Lord⟩ — like one who is disobedient through disbelief or otherwise? ﴿Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?⟩ meaning the two are not equal, just as the knower and the ignorant are not equal. ﴿Only those of understanding remember⟩ meaning take heed, ﴿those of understanding⟩ meaning the people of intellects.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 10:

﴿Say: O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord﴾, i.e., His punishment, by obeying Him. ﴿For those who do good in this world﴾ through obedience, ﴿there is a good [reward]﴾, which is Paradise. ﴿And the earth of Allah is spacious﴾, so emigrate to it from among the disbelievers and from witnessing the evil deeds. ﴿Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account﴾ for their patience in obedience and in what they are tested with, ﴿without measure or scale﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 11:

﴿Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ from associating partners with Him (min ash-shirk).
{And I have been commanded} i.e., to {be the first of the Muslims} of this community.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 14:

﴿Say, "It is Allah I worship, sincere to Him in my religion"﴾ from polytheism.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 15:

﴿Worship what you will besides Him﴾ (i.e., other than Him). This is a threat to them, and a declaration that they do not worship Allah, the Exalted.

﴿Say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾ by the eternal abiding of their souls in the Fire, and by their not reaching the maidens of paradise (al-ḥūr al-ʿīn) prepared for them in the Garden, had they believed. ﴿Verily, that is the manifest loss﴾ (al-mubīn), that is, the clear one.

﴿For them there will be canopies of fire above them﴾, layers (ṭibāq) ﴿and canopies below them﴾, of fire. ﴿That is what Allah frightens His servants with﴾, i.e., the believers, ﴿so that they fear Him﴾, ﴿indicates it﴾.
Those who avoid the ṭāghūt (false deities, i.e. the idols) from worshipping them, and turn penitently (anābū, i.e. they turn back) to God, theirs is the good news (al-bushrā, i.e. of Paradise).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 18:

﴿Those who listen to the word and follow the best of it.﴾ That is, what is good for them. ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding.﴾ The possessors of intellects.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 19:

﴿Is then he against whom the word of punishment has come (i.e., ﴿I will surely fill Hell﴾ — the verse...)﴾ ...

Let me restate this cleanly, since my first attempt above was not a faithful translation. Here is the complete rendering:

﴿Is he then, upon whom the word of punishment has become due, (that is:) ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you all﴾ and so on [the verse], ﴿will you then save﴾ rescue ﴿those who are in the Fire﴾? The answer to the conditional is implied, and the apparent noun has been placed in the position of the pronoun. The hamza is for denial, and the meaning is: you cannot guide him, so that you could rescue him from the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 20:

﴿But for those who have feared their Lord⦆ by obeying Him, ﴿there are lofty chambers above them, with lofty chambers built above them, beneath which rivers flow﴾, i.e., beneath the upper and lower chambers. ﴿It is the promise of Allah﴾, accusative by its implied verb. ﴿Allah does not fail in His promise﴾, His promise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 21:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ (i.e., do you not know) ﴿that Allah sent down water from the sky, and He threaded it as springs﴾ (i.e., He made it enter into the places of springs) ﴿in the earth. Then He brings out by it crops of varying colors. Then it withers﴾ (i.e., dries up) ﴿and you see it﴾ (after its greenness, for example) ﴿yellow. Then He makes it into debris﴾ (i.e., crumbled bits) ﴿Indeed in that is a reminder﴾ (i.e., an admonition) ﴿for those of understanding﴾ (who are mindful through it, by its indication of the Oneness of Allah, exalted is He, and His power).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 22:

﴿Is he whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam, so that he is upon a light from his Lord…?﴾ (the implied answer being: no, he is not like the one whose heart is sealed). The phrase "so that he is guided" (fa-ihtada) is understood here; ﴿then he is upon a light from his Lord﴾ is like "the one whose heart has been sealed," which indicates this (meaning). ﴿Woe﴾ (wayl) is a word for punishment ﴿to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah﴾, i.e., from accepting the Qur'an. ﴿They are in manifest error﴾, clear.

Allah has sent down the most beautiful statement, a Book (kitāban) in apposition (badal) to "aḥsan," meaning the Qur'an, ﴿consisting of parts resembling one another﴾, i.e., some of it resembles other parts in its composition and otherwise, ﴿oft-repeated﴾, meaning that the promise, the threat, and other matters are repeated within it. ﴿The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver at it﴾, i.e., they tremble at the mention of its threat. ﴿Then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾, i.e., they become tranquil (taṭma'inn) at the mention of His promise. ﴿That﴾, i.e., the Book, ﴿is the guidance of Allah; He guides with it whom He wills.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 24:

﴿Is one who shields with his face from the worst of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection﴾ (yalqa, i.e., will meet) ﴿bi-wajhihi sū' al-ʿadhāb yawm al-qiyāmah﴾ — that is, its worst form, by being cast into the Fire with his hands chained to his neck — ﴿like one who is secure from it by entering Paradise?﴾ ﴿It will be said to the wrongdoers﴾ — that is, the disbelievers of Makkah — ﴿Taste what you used to earn﴾ — that is, its recompense.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 25:

﴿Those before them denied﴾ their messengers concerning the coming of the punishment, ﴿so the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive﴾, from a direction that did not occur to their minds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 26:

﴿So Allah made them taste disgrace in the life of this world﴾ — the humiliation and abasement, from being transformed (into animals) and from being killed and other things. ﴿But the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew﴾ — i.e., the deniers, ﴿if only they knew﴾ its punishment, they would not have denied.
The Qur'an, "And We have certainly set forth": We made. "For the people in this Qur'an every kind of example, that perhaps they may remember": that perhaps they may take heed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 28:

﴿Qur'anan 'arabiyyan﴾ (a Qur'an in Arabic): a confirmatory circumstantial clause (ḥāl mu'akkada). ﴿Ghayra dhī 'iwaj﴾ (without any crookedness): i.e., without ambiguity (labs) or contradiction (ikhtilaf). ﴿La'allahum yattaqūn﴾ (so that they may guard themselves): against disbelief (al-kufr).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 29:

﴿God strikes⁠ ﴾ a parable for the polytheist and the monotheist: ﴿a man﴾ (a substitution for "a parable") ﴿in whom are partners at odds with one another﴾ (quarrelling with one another, their characters being bad), ﴿and a man wholly devoted⁠﴾ (purely, exclusively) ﴿to one man. Are the two equal in parable?⁠﴾ (a specification: that is, the slave belonging to a group is not equal to the slave belonging to one person, for the first, when each of his two masters demands his service at the same time, is bewildered as to which of them to serve. This is a parable for the polytheist, and the second is a parable for the monotheist.) ﴿Praise be to God⁠﴾ alone. ﴿But most of them⁠﴾ (i.e., the people of Mecca) ﴿do not know⁠﴾ the punishment to which they will come, so they associate partners with Him.

﴿Indeed you﴾ is an address to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿you are dying, and indeed they are dying﴾. That is, you will die and they will die, so there is no gloating over death. It was revealed when they were impatiently awaiting his (ﷺ) death.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 31:

﴿Then indeed you﴾ O people, among yourselves, concerning the acts of injustice you commit against one another.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 32:

﴿Then who﴾ means: there is no one ﴿more unjust than he who lies against Allah﴾ by ascribing to Him a partner and a son, ﴿and denies the truth﴾ meaning the Qur'an ﴿when it has come to him. Is there not in Hell an abode﴾ meaning a dwelling place ﴿for the disbelievers?﴾ Yes, there is.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 33:

﴿And the one who brings the truth﴾ is the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿and believes in it﴾ are the believers. So "the one" (alladhi) here carries the meaning of "those" (alladhina). ﴿They are the God-fearing﴾ (al-muttaqun) — [those who guard themselves against] shirk (associating partners with God).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 39, verse 34:

﴿They shall have whatever they wish with their Lord; that is the reward of the good-doers﴾ "for themselves," by their faith.

﴿That Allah may remove from them the worst of what they did and reward them their recompense according to the best of what they used to do.﴾

أسْوَأ وأَحْسَن بِمَعْنى السَّيِّئ والحَسَن
*"Aswa'" (أسوأ) and "ahsan" (أحسن) mean "al-sayyi'" (السيئ, the bad) and "al-hasan" (الحسن, the good).*

Translation of the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 39, verse 36:

﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾ That is, the Prophet (ﷺ). "Yes [He is]." ﴿And they threaten you﴾ — the address is to him — ﴿with those [idols] other than Him﴾, that is, the idols, [threatening] that they will kill him or afflict him with madness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 37:

﴿And whoever Allah guides, for him there is no misleader. Is not Allah the Mighty, the Lord of Retribution?﴾ Mighty: overpowering over His affair. ﴿Lord of Retribution﴾: taking vengeance upon His enemies? Yes indeed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 38:

﴿Wa-la-in﴾ the lam is a lam of oath (lam al-qasam) ﴿sa'altahum man khalaqa al-samawati wal-ard la-yaqulunna Allah﴾ ("If you asked them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they would surely say, 'Allah.'") ﴿Qul ara'aytum ma tad'una﴾ ("Say: 'Have you considered what you invoke") ﴿ta'buduna﴾ (worship) ﴿min dun Allah﴾ (besides Allah)? ﴿ay al-asnam﴾ (i.e., the idols) ﴿in aradani Allah bi-durrin hal hunna kashifat durrihi﴾ ("if Allah intends harm for me, can they remove His harm?") — no; ﴿aw aradani bi-rahmatin hal hunna mumsikat rahmatihi﴾ ("or if He intends mercy for me, can they withhold His mercy?") — no. And in one reading, with the idafah (genitive construction) in both places: "kashifatu durrihi" and "mumsikatu rahmatihi." ﴿Qul hasbiya Allah, 'alayhi yatawakkal al-mutawakkilun﴾ ("Say: 'Allah is sufficient for me; in Him put their trust those who trust.'") — yathiqu al-wathiqun (those who rely firmly rely).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 39, verse 39:

﴿Say: "O my people, act according to your station,"﴾ meaning, according to your state, ﴿"indeed I am acting,"﴾ according to my state.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 39, verse 40:

﴿مَن﴾ is a relative pronoun (*mawsulah*), and it is the object of *al-'ilm* (knowledge), meaning the object of "you will know" in the previous verse. ﴿Whoever﴾ ﴿will receive a punishment that disgraces him, and there will descend﴾ ﴿upon him a lasting punishment﴾ that is perpetual. It is the punishment of the Fire. And God did disgrace them at Badr.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 41:

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind in truth﴾ — the phrase "in truth" (bil-haqq) is connected to "sent down" (anzala).

﴿So whoever is guided, it is for his own soul that he is guided﴾ — his guidance benefits himself.

﴿And whoever goes astray, he only goes astray to its detriment﴾ — and whoever goes astray, he only strays to his own harm, ﴿and you are not a guardian over them﴾ — so that you would compel them to guidance.

Allah takes the souls at the time of death, and those that have not died [He takes] in their sleep (﴿الَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنامها﴾), that is, He takes them at the time of sleep. ﴿Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death, and sends the others back until an appointed term.﴾ That is, until the time of their death. The one that is sent back is the soul of discernment (nafs al-tamyiz), which remains when the soul of life (nafs al-hayah) is absent, but not the reverse. ﴿Indeed in that﴾ mentioned [process] ﴿are signs﴾, proofs, ﴿for a people who reflect﴾, so that they know that the One who is able to do that is able to resurrect, and the Quraysh did not reflect upon that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 43:

﴿Am﴾ (rather/or), ﴿they have taken intercessors besides Allah﴾, i.e., idols as gods, ﴿intercessors﴾ with Allah, according to their assumption. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Even though they possess nothing, nor do they understand?﴾ They do not possess intercession or anything else, and they do not understand that you worship them or anything besides that. No!

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 44:

﴿Say: "To Allah belongs all intercession."﴾ That is: it is exclusively His, so no one intercedes except by His permission.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 45:

﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned﴾, i.e., without their gods, ﴿the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter recoil﴾, i.e., they are repelled and constricted, ﴿and when those besides Him are mentioned﴾, i.e., the idols,

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 46:

﴿Say: "O Allah"﴾ meaning: O Allah (yā Allāh), ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, the one who brought them into being without precedent, ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, what is hidden and what is observed. ﴿You will judge between Your servants concerning that in which they used to differ﴾ of matters of religion. "Guide me to the truth in what they have differed over."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 47:

﴿And if those who did wrong had everything on earth, and the same again with it, they would surely offer it as ransom from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from Allah what they had not reckoned﴾ — appeared, [i.e., became manifest] to them — ﴿what they had not reckoned﴾ — [i.e., did not expect/suppose].
And there appeared to them the evils of what they had earned, and there befell them [what they used to mock] — that is, the punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 49:

﴿So when harm touches the human being﴾ (al-insan, i.e. the species) ﴿he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favour from Us﴾ (i.e., We give him a blessing as a kindness) ﴿he says: "I have only been given it on account of knowledge"﴾ (from Allah, that I deserve it) ﴿Nay, it is a trial﴾ (i.e., this saying) ﴿a tribulation by which the servant is tested﴾ ﴿but most of them do not know﴾ that the bestowing is a gradual lead-on (istidraj) and a test.
Qad qālahā alladhīna min qablihim (﴿Those before them had already said it﴾) — from the nations, like Qarun and his people, who were content with it.

﴿So the evils of what they had earned afflicted them.﴾ That is, their recompense. ﴿And as for those who wronged among these people,﴾ that is, the Quraysh, ﴿the evils of what they earned will afflict them, and they will not escape,﴾ meaning they will not get away from Our punishment. So they were struck with famine for seven years, then they were given abundance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 52:

﴿Did they not know that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it?﴾ He widens it for whomever He wills as a trial (imtihanan). ﴿And restricts it﴾ He narrows it for whomever He wills as a test (ibtila'). ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ in Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 53:

﴿Say: "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins."﴾ [The verb] "taqnatū" is read with a kasra and with a fatḥa on the nūn; it is also read with a ḍamma (taqnaṭū), and in the variant reading [it is] "tay'asū" (you despair). ﴿of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾ for whoever repents from polytheism (shirk).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 39, verse 54:

﴿And turn back in repentance﴾ return ﴿to your Lord and submit to Him﴾ make your deeds sincerely for Him ﴿before the punishment comes upon you, and then you will not be helped﴾ to prevent it, if you do not repent.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 55:

﴿And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ — it is the Qur'an — ﴿before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive﴾ — before its coming at its time.

Then turn to your Lord in repentance before ﴿a soul says, "Oh, my regret over what I neglected in regard to Allah"﴾. Its original form is "yā ḥasratī," meaning my regret (nadāmatī), ﴿over what I neglected in regard to Allah﴾, meaning His obedience. ﴿And indeed﴾ is the lightened form of the heavy one (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), meaning "and indeed I", ﴿was among those who mocked﴾ His religion and His Book.
﴿Or [lest] you say, "If only Allah had guided me"﴾ [to] obedience, ﴿so I would have been guided﴾, ﴿and I would have been among the righteous﴾ [who fear] His punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 58:

﴿Or [lest] it say, when it sees the punishment: "If only I had a return [to the world], so that I could be among the good-doers"﴾ — a return to the world — ﴿among the good-doers﴾, the believers. Then it will be said to him from God:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 59:

﴿Yes, indeed, My signs came to you﴾ — the Qur'an, which is the means of guidance — ﴿but you denied them and were arrogant﴾ — you became proud, refusing to believe in them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 60:

﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah﴾ by ascribing to Him a partner and a son, ﴿their faces blackened.﴾ ﴿Is there not in Hell an abode﴾ (maʼwa, a dwelling place) ﴿for the arrogant?﴾ (ʼarrogant toward faith) ﴿Yes indeed.﴾

Allah will deliver (ﷻ) from Hell ﴿those who were mindful of (their duty to Allah)﴾ by avoiding shirk (associating partners with Allah), ﴿with their salvation﴾, i.e., by means of their place of triumph from the Garden, by being placed in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 62:

﴿Allah is the Creator of every thing, and He is, over every thing, a Disposer of affairs.﴾ He disposes of it however He wills.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 63:

﴿To Him belong the keys (maqalid) of the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., the keys to their treasuries of rain, plants and other things. ﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿those are the losers﴾. This is connected to His saying: ﴿And Allah will save those who feared Him﴾, and so on, and what lies between them is an interjection (i'tirad).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 64:

﴿Say: Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, you ignorant ones?﴾ Ghayr (other than) is in the accusative, governed by ṭa'budu (worship), which is the object of ta'murūnnī (you order me), with an implied an (that) before it. [It is read] with one nūn (ta'murūnī) and with two nūns, assimilated (idghām) and unassimilated (fakk).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 65:

﴿And indeed it has been revealed to you and to those before you﴾ — and by Allah — ﴿that if you should associate [others with Allah], your work would surely be nullified﴾ — O Muhammad — supposing [for the sake of argument].
﴿Rather, Allah﴾ alone ﴿so worship [Him], and be among the thankful﴾ for His blessing upon you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 67:

﴿They did not measure God with His true measure﴾: they did not know Him with His true knowledge, or they did not glorify Him with His true glory, when they associated others with Him. ﴿And the earth entirely⦅will be⦆ in His grip﴾: a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), i.e., the seven [earths] ﴿in His grip﴾: i.e., held in His grasp, that is, in His dominion and disposal ﴿on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens folded up⦅will be⦆﴾: gathered together ﴿in His right hand﴾: by His power ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾: [above] those [partners] they associate with Him.

﷽

﴿And the Trumpet will be blown﴾, the first blowing, ﴿and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon﴾, meaning die, ﴿except whom God wills﴾ of the Houris and the wildan (youths of Paradise) and others.

﴿Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾, meaning all the dead creatures will be standing, awaiting what will be done to them.

And the earth shall shine with the light of its Lord, when Allah appears to judge between the creatures. And the Book (the book of deeds) shall be placed for the reckoning. And the prophets and the witnesses shall be brought, that is, Muhammad (ﷺ) and his community, who will bear witness for the messengers that they conveyed the message. And judgment shall be passed between them with truth, that is, with justice, and they shall not be wronged in anything.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 70:

﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did﴾, i.e., its recompense, ﴿and He is most knowing﴾, knowing ﴿of what they do﴾, so He has no need of a witness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 71:

﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups﴾ violently, ﴿in separate groups﴾ bands dispersed one after another. ﴿Until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened﴾ the answer to "when" (idhā) is the phrase that follows. ﴿And its keepers will say to them, "Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord﴾ the Qur'an and other than it, ﴿and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has been justified"﴾ meaning: ﴿"I will surely fill Hell"﴾ and the rest of the verse.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 72:

﴿It is said: "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein forever."﴾ [They are] intending to abide forever. ﴿Wretched is the abode of the arrogant.﴾ [That is,] Hell is the dwelling place (ma'wa) [of] the arrogant.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 73:

﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups﴾ gently, ﴿until, when they reach it and its gates have been opened﴾. The waw here is for the circumstantial clause, with qad implied. ﴿And its keepers will say to them: Peace be upon you; you have been good﴾ is a circumstantial clause. ﴿So enter it, abiding eternally﴾, intending to abide in it forever. The answer to "when" (idha) is omitted, meaning: their entry, their being driven, and the opening of the gates (before their arrival) is an honour for them; while the driving of the disbelievers and the opening of the gates of Hell upon their arrival is for their humiliation, so that its heat remains upon them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 74:

﴿And they will say﴾ It is conjoined to their entry (into Paradise), which is implied: ﴿"All praise is due to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us"﴾ of Paradise ﴿and has caused us to inherit the earth﴾, i.e., the land of Paradise, ﴿so that we may settle﴾ dwell ﴿in Paradise wherever we will﴾, because all of it is such that no place in it is preferred over another ﴿How excellent is the reward of those who work﴾, namely Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 39, verse 75:

﴿And you will see the angels circling around the Throne﴾ (ḥāl) ﴿from all around it﴾, from every side of it. ﴿Glorifying﴾ (ḥāl from the pronoun in ḥāffīn) ﴿with the praise of their Lord﴾ (mulābisīna lil-ḥamd), i.e., they say: "Glory be to Allah and with His praise." ﴿And it will be judged between them﴾ between all of creation ﴿with truth﴾, i.e., with justice, so the believers will enter Paradise and the disbelievers the Fire. ﴿And it will be said: "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ This is the conclusion of the settling of both groups, with praise from the angels.
